name: Thick ascending limb
summary: The diluting segment. Actively reabsorbs about 25% of filtered NaCl through NKCC2 but is impermeable to water, so fluid leaves it hypotonic (~100 mOsm) and the salt it pumps out makes the medulla hypertonic (the countercurrent multiplier). K⁺ recycling through ROMK makes the lumen positive, which drives Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ reabsorption between the cells. Loop diuretics block NKCC2; Bartter syndrome is a genetic version. Makes uromodulin (Tamm–Horsfall protein, the matrix of casts); its macula densa senses NaCl for tubuloglomerular feedback and renin release.
tissue: kidney: loop of Henle, thick ascending limb (outer medulla and cortex)

na_l.name: Na⁺ (lumen)
na_l.notes: About 25% of filtered Na⁺ is reabsorbed here.

nkcc2.name: NKCC2 (Na⁺–K⁺–2Cl⁻ cotransporter)
nkcc2.notes: Carries Na⁺, K⁺ and 2 Cl⁻ into the cell. Loop diuretics (furosemide, bumetanide, torsemide, ethacrynic acid) block it: up to 25% of filtered Na⁺ escapes, the medullary gradient collapses, and more Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ are lost (“loops lose calcium”). Bartter syndrome type 1 (looks like taking a loop diuretic).

nak.name: Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase
nak.notes: On the basolateral side of every tubular cell: 3 Na⁺ out, 2 K⁺ in, using ATP. Keeping cell Na⁺ low is what drives every apical Na⁺ carrier (secondary active transport).

clckb.name: ClC-Kb (chloride channel)
clckb.notes: Basolateral Cl⁻ channel that needs its partner barttin to work. Loss of either: Bartter syndrome (types 3 and 4).

romk.name: ROMK (K⁺ channel)
romk.notes: Lets K⁺ back into the lumen so NKCC2 never runs short of K⁺, and makes the lumen positive, which pushes Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ out between the cells. Bartter syndrome type 2.

para.name: Paracellular (lumen-positive voltage)
para.notes: The lumen-positive voltage drives Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ between the cells, through tight junctions made of claudin-16 and claudin-19 (their loss: familial hypomagnesemia with hypercalciuria). Loop diuretics remove the voltage, so more Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ are lost.

drugs.name: Loop diuretics
drugs.note: Block NKCC2: furosemide, bumetanide, torsemide, ethacrynic acid. Edema; hypokalemia, ototoxicity; they make you lose calcium.

diseases.name: Bartter syndrome
diseases.clue: Hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis with high urinary calcium in a child: looks like taking a loop diuretic.
